title: The Hollow Protocol Again
premise: Wendell Ashgrove, a navigator who fled the war after discovering her own backup sleeping in her ship's hold, is conscripted to escort a vessel whose crew returned from deep space biologically reversed — living proof that the enemy's immortality protocol works. The message she carries contains the protocol's fatal flaw: it erases memory faster than it restores bodies, meaning every 'saved' soldier becomes someone new. When both fleets converge on the relay station where she must broadcast it, Wendell must choose between destroying the backups — including her own — or letting humanity trade its past for endless tomorrows. She broadcasts the truth and burns the hold, choosing an unrepeatable life with the found family aboard her ship.
about_author: Hazel Winterbourne is a former maritime radio operator who writes science fiction about people who keep transmissions running when no one is listening. She lives on a houseboat with three cats and a wall of obsolete navigation equipment.

chapters.title: Cargo in Contested Space
chapters.summary: Wendell navigates a routine haul through a blockade while her crew — engineer Sefa, pilot Bo, and stowaway medic Idris — bicker over dinner. A distress ping from a ship that vanished seven years ago overrides her console. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: weary competence masking guilt about the sealed backup bay she never opens.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Back Young
chapters.summary: They dock with the derelict Meridian and find its crew aged backward into children and young adults, memories intact but bodies decades younger. One survivor, Captain Oyelaran, recognizes Wendell's name from the war. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: horror curdling into recognition — the protocol she ran from has come back wearing familiar faces.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Oyelaran reveals the message hidden in Meridian's black box and begs Wendell to deliver it to the neutral relay at Kestrel Station. Flashbacks show how Wendell discovered her own backup five years ago and deserted. POV: Wendell with one flashback interlude. Emotional beat: shame confronted; the crew votes to take the job, binding them together.

chapters.title: Sefa's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: En route, Sefa decodes part of the message and finds coordinates for a backup vault holding thousands of copies of war-dead soldiers. Bo, who lost his brother in the war, wants to retrieve him. POV: Bo. Emotional beat: hope as a dangerous drug; first fracture in the found family.

chapters.title: Interdiction at the Shoals
chapters.summary: A Republic patrol board their ship hunting the Meridian survivors. Wendell bluffs them off using her old military clearance, but they're flagged. Idris quietly treats a deteriorating child-crew member, learning the reversal is unstable. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: tenderness under pressure; the cost of carrying other people's secrets.

chapters.title: The Vault of the Unburied
chapters.summary: Diverting to the vault, Bo finds his brother's backup — but waking it produces a man with the brother's face and none of his shared memories. Bo must decide whether love survives translation. POV: Bo. Emotional beat: grief reframed; he lets the copy sleep and grieves properly for the first time.

chapters.title: Kestrel Station Lockdown
chapters.summary: Arriving at Kestrel, they find the relay seized by a faction that wants the message destroyed because it ends the profitable stalemate. Wendell's old commander offers her amnesty in exchange for the black box. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: temptation of a clean slate versus loyalty to the crew waiting in the docking bay.

chapters.title: Every Version of Me
chapters.summary: Cornered, Wendell confronts her own backup, awakened by the faction as leverage. Talking with herself, she realizes the message's truth: the protocol doesn't preserve people, it replaces them. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: self-reckoning; she stops running from who she was and chooses who she'll be.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. The crew runs a suicide-run through the station's defenses while Wendell reaches the transmitter. Both fleets arrive; she broadcasts the full message — the flaw, the vaults, the erased minds — forcing both sides to see what victory would cost. Oyelaran dies shielding the antenna. POV: alternating Wendell and Sefa. Emotional beat: sacrifice and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Unrepeatable
chapters.summary: A fragile ceasefire holds as both fleets reckon with the truth. Wendell destroys her own backup in the hold, and the crew — plus the surviving child-crew of Meridian, now theirs to raise — sets course for open space. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; survival without repetition, family chosen over continuity.
